newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakhstan's Irtysh copper smelter restarts output.
newsitem.headline: Kazakhstan's Irtysh copper smelter restarts output.

text.p: Kazakhstan's Irtysh copper smelter, in a venture with British firm Dayton Associates Ltd, has restarted output and aims to produce about 3,000 tonnes of blister copper per month, the plant's director said on Friday.
The smelter, with a capacity of around 40,000 tonnes per year and located in the northeast of the vast former Soviet republic, had been idle for several months.
"In the near future (April), the plant plans to produce about 3,000 tonnes a month of blister copper," Leonid Budovsky, the smelter's director, told Reuters by telephone.
He said a sharp fall in copper prices and rising production costs had forced the smelter to shutter operations.
But Budovsky said Dayton Associates, which won a tender for the enterprise, had pledged to invest $35 million in the venture over four years.
According to the official daily Kazakhstanskaya Pravda, Dayton paid $1.0 million for the smelter.

"The investment programme is in two stages," Budovsky said. "In the first stage, which will take about four years, it is planned to rehabilitate the smelter and increase production to 60,000 tonnes per year."

He said the second stage would see production nearly doubled to 100,000 tonnes per year of copper cathode. Copper concentrates are currently sourced from local mines. --Tatyana Seroshtanova, Almaty Newsroom +7 3272 509410
